title: GLM native search recurrence exposes lost server-tool observations and replay-contract ambiguity
wanted_capability: Explain and correctly handle GLM native search protocol blocks during ordinary code tasks. Preserve actual server executions in durable observations and replay provider-owned blocks without fabricating client results. Determine placeholder invocation cause from request/response evidence before selecting a repair; a tool deny list is not a protocol fix.
fallback_used: Inspected transport snapshots because durable event logs omit the server-tool blocks. Root withdrew the filter-only explanation and dispatched protocol investigation.

notes: Confirmed replay and durable-observation defects are repaired in commits 624c8603 and 8c01614d; native input_schema is limited to the MiniMax protocol variation. Full workspace verification at e7985322 passed 6684 tests. Canonical and GLM server blocks have replay and log regressions. The cause of placeholder search initiation remains unproven; neither a query deny list nor capability disablement is the repair. Fresh provider probes on 2026-09-06 at 20:49:11 UTC (glm-5.3) and 20:57:24 UTC (glm-5.3-flash) returned HTTP 429 code 1308, explicitly a five-hour quota cap. The reset timestamp did not carry a timezone. Successful provider-level confirmation remains outstanding. Follow-up at 2026-09-06T21:46:50Z again directly observed Flash HTTP429/code1308. Native-search scrutiny found and reproduced lost tool_search activation on process resume; this is correlated with both saved incidents, but provider query-selection causality remains unproven. No query deny list or default search disablement was added. Live allocator preview separately attributed no_candidates to an expired runtime-rate-limit exclusion.
